sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (for short, 'the Corporation') of the offending vehicle challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal as excessive and seeking reduction of the same and also on negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing registered No.KA-27/H-6513.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and respondents.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matters are taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

4. The Corporation has filed this appeal to modify/set aside the judgment and award in MVC No.19/2016 date 04.11.2017 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge and A.M.A.C.T.,
Ranebennur.
The brief facts of the claimants case before the Tribunal is as under, on 19.06.2015 at about 7.30 P.M. the deceased was proceedings with claimant in motorcycle bearing registered No.KA-27/H-6513.

The claimant was rider of motorcycle, who was riding the same on P.B.road,
Davanagere, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registered No.KA-17/1693 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the claimant.

Due to the said impact,
claimant sustained injuries.
6. Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
Aggrieved by the judgment and award of the Tribunal the Corporation preferred this appeal, challenging the quantum of compensation as well as negligence.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants/Corporation contended that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.

But it is only negligence on the part of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7807 claimant/respondent.
The amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

Hence, he prayed to modify the judgment and award of the Tribunal by reducing the The Managing Director, K.S.R.T.C vs Sri. Ramesh S/O Tammanna Lamani on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123938068/
2 compensation.
8.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, has granted fair and reasonable compensation.
However, the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bus and hence, the entire liability is saddled upon the Corporation.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
9.

In view of the submission made by both counsel and materials available on record, the following points that would arise for the Court consideration in this appeal are:
"Whether the Corporation proved that the rider of motorcycle also contributed negligence and hence, Corporation is not liable to pay entire compensation?"
"Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or does it call for enhancement?"
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7807 10.
In order to substantiate the contention of the Corporation, the Corporation got examined Sri.Gnaneshwara S/o Ramachandra Rao Doddamani as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R.1-Authoriation letter.
On the other hand, the claimants examined as PW.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 44.

As per the contents of Ex.P.1-FIR, Ex.P.2-complaint, Ex.P.3-Re-statement of complaint, Ex.P.4-Spot Panchanama, Ex.P.5-IMV Report and Ex.P.6- Inquest Panchanama etc., it shows that the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registered No.KA-17/F-1693 came in a rash and negligent manner in order to endanger the human life, dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased and caused the accident.

The oral evidence of PW.2 is supported by documentary evidence at Exs.P.1 to P.6.
11.
It is not disputed by the appellant that the accident was occurred on 19.06.2015 at about 7.30 P.M.
The Corporation has not challenged the documents and oral evidence of PW.2.

The oral and documentary evidence clearly establishes that, the accident was occurred due to NC:
2024:KHC-D:7807 rash and negligent driving of driver of the KSRTC bus.
Hence, the Corporation is liable to pay the compensation.
12. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation at Rs.20,000/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum.
Hence, no interference is called for in respect of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
13. Hence, there is no merit in the appeal and accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
